configs.description: Dual AC PSUs, back-to-front airflow. The vendor's product page offers "front-to-back or back-to-front airflow options"; THIS DEVICE'S OWN GUIDE DOES NOT STATE THE COLOUR RULE, so the blue handles and latches are this line's convention applied here rather than a quotation. See roc-ops/Portrayal#277.

configs.name: ac-f2b

gaps.wanted: A drawing of the lid, the underside and the two side walls. Nothing in this corpus draws any of them flat - the mounting figures show brackets going on in three-quarter view, and the -FF photograph is a three-quarter of the front. Each carries an `empty:` sentence saying where I looked, per docs/deliberately-empty-faces.md.

The second lamp on each OSFP port. The System LEDs enlargement resolves FOUR triangles under each column - two up for the upper port and two down for the lower - and the guide names both: a left lamp carrying seven rate and breakout modes, and a right lamp carrying link, activity and a blinking red for "no link on one or more ports". One per port is drawn and it carries the LEFT lamp's vocabulary, because that is the one that says what the port is doing. Drawing both would be 32 placements and 32 cutouts, and edgecore/dcs240, edgecore/dcs201 and edgecore/as5912-54x all make the same simplification on the same kind of cluster.

One chassis size. The datasheet says 442 x 509 x 44 mm and the quick start's own hardware table says 438.4 x 589 x 43.1 - eighty millimetres of depth apart, with both self-consistent in inches, so neither is a typo. The datasheet's figures are used because the live vendor page agrees with them and because both of the guide's own elevations scale to a round 5 px/mm at 442 and to nothing in particular at 438.4. A DEPTH IS THE LEAST TESTABLE OF THE THREE and this model draws no side view, so nothing here would catch it if the guide is the right one. The weights disagree the same way, 10.005 kg against 13.48 kg with PSUs and fans installed.

Whether the 1PPS jack is an SMA or an SMB. The datasheet names it "1PPS SMA connector"; the elevation draws it 5.00 x 5.44 mm, where common/sma-jack@1 is 9.5 across flats and edgecore/dcs510 measures its own SMA nuts at 8.6. common/smb-jack@1 is seated because it is what fits the drawing, and seating the SMA envelope would overlap the LOC lamp 0.6 mm away. A caliper on the real jack settles it in one measurement.

Whether a DC supply exists. The datasheet says only "AC PSUs: 1+1 redundancy, load-sharing, hot-swappable" and the quick start "2 x AC PSUs"; no DC variant is named anywhere, and no ordering table is staged for this model. The other Edgecore data-centre switches in this library all offer both, so its absence here is recorded rather than assumed either way. Only AC configurations are declared.

a `power-draw-max-w` on each module this chassis accepts, from the vendor's own per-card table - Cisco publishes one per ambient, most vendors publish none, and until they land a module total is a floor

one of `power-max-w`, `power-max-ac-w`, `power-max-dc-w` in a missing `attrs.power` section (profile `networking` - see spec/schemas/profiles.yaml) - unlocks the About panel, and comparison against other devices
`physical-context` on 8 bays (rear 8); `physical-context` on port group osfp - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays

gate-1.note: THE TWO ELEVATIONS ARE NOT EQUALLY GOOD, AND NEITHER IS THE PHOTOGRAPH'S BOUNDING BOX. Both Overview elevations on page 1 are orthographic - the front's width samples 2407 px at seven heights with no taper - and both are drawn at very close to exactly 5 px/mm when scaled by 442 mm: the front is 2211 px wide (5.0023) and the rear 2207 (4.9932). Two drawings landing within 0.14% of a round 5.0 is itself evidence that 442 is the width they were drawn to. THE REAR IS THE GOOD DRAWING. It reads 2207 x 217 px, an aspect of 10.171 against the stated 442 / 43.94 = 10.059, 1.1% out. THE FRONT IS 5.3% OUT and squashed vertically: 2211 x 210 px gives 10.574. Its y axis is therefore NOT 5.0023 but 210 / 43.94 = 4.7791, and every front y below is read on that second scale. THAT CORRECTION IS NOT A FUDGE, AND THE APERTURE PROVES IT. At 5.0023 on both axes the OSFP openings read 22.59 x 12.59 against std/osfp@1's 23.1 x 13.5 - 2.2% under in x and 6.7% under in y, which is two different errors. At 5.0023 by 4.7791 they read 22.59 x 13.18: 2.2% and 2.4%, ONE error in both axes, which is a drawing whose cages are a little small rather than a drawing whose axes disagree.

lamps.note: quick start, System LEDs/Buttons, verbatim: "OSFP Left LED: Blue (2x400G), Cyan (1x400G), Green (4x200G), Magenta (2x200G), White (8x100G), Amber (4x100G), Red (8x50G)" and "OSFP Right LED: Green/Blinking (link/activity), Blinking Red (no link on one or more ports)". Also "RJ-45 MGMT LEDs: Left: Amber (link), Right: Green (activity)". SEVEN BREAKOUT MODES ON THE LEFT LAMP, which is the rate indicator, and the right lamp is link/activity. ONE LAMP PER PORT IS DRAWN AND THE METAL HAS TWO - the enlargement shows four triangles under each column, two pointing up for the top port and two down for the bottom. The drawn lamp carries the LEFT lamp's seven-mode vocabulary as states, because that is the one that says what the port is doing. The gap below records the other. THE LAMPS ARE TRIANGLES, not dots: up-pointing for the upper row and down for the lower, which is what common/led-arrow@1's two skins are for.

power.note: 863 W MAXIMUM, AND IT IS NOT IN EITHER STAGED DOCUMENT. The vendor's product page states "863W" as the maximum power draw. The datasheet gives only "AC Input Voltage: 90 to 240 VAC at 50-60 Hz" and the quick start only the system input rating, "100-120 VAC, 50/60 Hz, 12 A max. per PS / 200-240 VAC, 50/60 Hz, 7.5 A max. per PS". NO PER-SUPPLY OUTPUT RATING IS PUBLISHED ANYWHERE, so edgecore/exp800-psu-ac@1 carries no `power-output-w`. Multiplying the input maxima out would be inventing a figure the vendor does not claim.

sources.note: Two documents and five photographs, all staged, plus one live vendor page. exp800-16o-qsg and exp800-16o-datasheet, both docling-converted and MEASURED OFF THE PDF PAGE at 600 dpi rather than off the converted figures. working/intake/edgecore/photos/ holds exp800-16o-2-EXP800-16O-F.webp and -3-EXP800-16O-B.webp, square-on shots of both faces, plus an angled -A, a second -A as PNG and a three-quarter -FF. THE VENDOR PAGE WAS CONSULTED AND IT EARNED ITS PLACE: www.edge-core.com/product/exp800-16o/ states a maximum power draw of 863 W, and NEITHER staged document states a consumption figure at all. Without it this model would carry a gap where it can carry a number.

the-bay-digits-are-drawable-here.note: AND ON THIS LINE'S OTHER CHASSIS THEY ARE NOT, which is worth saying because edgecore/csr440 and edgecore/dcs511 both carry a gap for exactly this. Those devices put six 48.5 mm trays on a 48.50 mm pitch, so their bays butt and the digits the metal prints between them land INSIDE a neighbouring bay box - silkscreen over a module, which L21 is right to refuse. THIS CHASSIS HAS RAILS. The bay seams fall in pairs about 7.4 mm apart, so 41.45 mm of tray alternates with 7.47 mm of chassis, and a digit at a rail's centre is on metal that belongs to no module. The digit for bay 2 resolves on the elevation at x 317.83-319.23, y 23.29-25.31, inside the rail that runs 315.03 to 322.44; the other five are placed at their own rail centres - 122.97, 171.94, 220.80, 269.87, 318.74 and 367.40 - which agree with the rear photograph's digit positions to better than a millimetre. EACH DIGIT NAMES THE BAY TO ITS LEFT. 6 sits in the rail right of the leftmost tray and 1 in the rail right of the rightmost, which is the order the panel prints and the reverse of the bays' left-to-right position.

the-management-stack.note: ONE HOUSING, TWO CONNECTORS, as on edgecore/dcs511. The bright bezel at the right of the port row reads x 355.44 to 371.83 and y 11.30 to 31.80 - 16.4 by 20.5 mm, which is a 1000BASE-T RJ-45 over a USB Type-A in one moulding rather than two bare parts. The datasheet lists them separately, "1 x RJ-45 1G BASE-T management" and "1 x USB Type A storage", and the panel prints MGMT and USB vertically beside the stack. There is no stacked RJ45/USB part in this library, so the housing is drawn as a decor under both, which is what the DCS511 does. THE CONSOLE IS SEPARATE AND ON THE OTHER SIDE, at x 57.97-74.77 by y 18.41-32.01 - 16.8 by 13.6 against std/rj45@2's 15.8 by 13.2 - with CONSOLE printed above it. One console here, where the DCS240 and DCS511 both carry two.

the-optical-wall.note: SIXTEEN PORTS AS EIGHT COLUMNS OF TWO, ON ONE UNIFORM PITCH. The cage openings segment cleanly as eight dark runs 113 px wide, and their steps are 160, 160, 162, 160, 160, 160 and 160 px - a single pitch of 31.99 mm with NO ganging and no gutter, which is what makes this wall different from the DCS240's eight blocks of two. Column 1 opens at 98.16 mm and the wall ends at 345.04. The openings read 22.59 mm wide against std/osfp@1's 23.1 and 13.18 tall against its 13.5, both about 2.3% under - see gate-1 for why that consistency is the check on the y scale rather than a defect. std/osfp@1's own size was measured on a UFISPACE drawing, not this one, so it is used as the part and NOT as a ruler for this face. ROWS: the upper opening runs 3.14 to 16.32 mm and the lower 18.20 to 31.38, a row pitch of 15.07.

the-photograph-includes-the-lid.note: A CORRECTION TO MY OWN FIRST READING, and the reason to distrust an ink bounding box. The front photograph's ink spans 104 rows, which at 960 px / 442 mm is 47.5 mm - taller than a 1RU and therefore impossible. I very nearly recorded the vertical axis as unusable on that basis. ROWS 296-301 ARE NOT THE FRONT FACE. They are a flat band of uniform grey, 89.6 to 89.9, whose colour saturation climbs from 3 to 20 while the panel below varies from 52 to 161. Magnified they are plainly the CHASSIS LID: the shot is taken very slightly from above. There is a similar sliver at the foot. Excluding them the face is 93 to 98 px depending on where the seam is placed - 42.8 to 45.1 mm, which brackets 43.94. So the photograph does not contradict the stated height at all; it was being measured lid-to-base. The same reading applies to edgecore/dcs511's photograph, whose 98-px box over a 95.3-px face was put down to edge highlight.

the-ports-start-at-zero.note: AND THIS IS THE ONLY EDGECORE DEVICE IN THE LIBRARY THAT DOES. The panel prints `0` above an up arrow and a down arrow above `1` beneath the first column, then `2`/`3`, and the System LEDs enlargement resolves the first pair at 600 dpi beyond argument. Sixteen ports numbered 0 to 15, two per column, numbering DOWN each column. `index-origin: 0` on the group and `number-from: 0` on the block. Every sibling in this line - the DCS240, the DCS511, the DCS201 - starts at 1, so this is the kind of fact a family carry-over silently destroys.

the-rear.note: MEASURED ON THE REAR ELEVATION, WHICH IS THE GOOD ONE, and confirmed on the photograph. PS1 IS ON THE LEFT AND PS2 ON THE RIGHT, which is the reverse of edgecore/dcs511 - the panel prints PS1 beside the left module and PS2 beside the right, each with an airflow arrow. Getting this from the sibling would have swapped them. The bay wall closes on itself. Both supply frames read 50.6 mm wide - PS1 at 16.0 to 66.6 and PS2 at 375.3 to 425.9 - leaving a left margin of 16.0 and a right of 16.1. The six fan bays sit between them with gaps of 11.1 and 11.4. THE FAN BAYS ARE SEPARATED BY A RAIL, which is why their module width and their pitch are different numbers. Seams fall in pairs about 7.4 mm apart, so the modules are 41.45 wide and the pitch is 48.92 - measured independently by colour-segmenting the six red pull bars, whose centres fit a 48.921 pitch with residuals of 0.18 mm or less. 41.45 plus 7.47 is 48.92. The photograph agrees at half the resolution: its bars fit a 49.30 pitch, 0.8% out.

the-system-lamps.note: FIVE WINDOWS, ALL ROUND, AND ALL FIVE ARE NAMED. The System LEDs enlargement on page 1 resolves Diag and PS1 on the top row, FAN and PS2 on the middle, and LOC alone on the bottom left - a 3+2 grid, every one a circle, every one labelled. The guide's own list names exactly the same five. THIS IS A REAL DIFFERENCE FROM THE SIBLINGS and was checked rather than assumed: the DCS240 and DCS511 both draw SIX windows of which one carries no legend anywhere, and the DCS240's right column is rectangular. Neither is true here. Positions off the elevation: left column centred x 81.26, right column x 89.46, rows at y 14.40, 17.60 and 20.90.

the-timing-jack-is-drawn-smaller-than-it.note: THE DATASHEET SAYS SMA AND THE DRAWING SAYS OTHERWISE. The datasheet's interface table reads "2. 1PPS SMA connector"; the quick start says only "1PPS timing port" and "Use a coax cable". BUT THE ELEVATION DRAWS A 5 MM JACK. Colour-segmenting the gold nut on the front elevation gives 5.00 x 5.44 mm centred at (85.36, 25.63). common/sma-jack@1 is 9.5 mm across flats - measured on a different vendor's drawing, and edgecore/dcs510 records its own SMA nuts at 8.6 mm. A 5 mm gold feature is not an SMA nut. SEATING THE SMA WOULD ALSO COLLIDE. At 9.5 across the part would span x 80.6-90.1 by y 20.9-30.4 and the LOC lamp sits at x 80.16-82.36, y 20.30-21.55 - inside it. L13 would be right to complain, and a drawing that leaves 0.6 mm between a nut and a lamp is telling us the nut is small. common/smb-jack@1 is seated, at 7.0 with a 4.83 aperture, because it is the part that fits what is drawn. The device's `timing` group carries the datasheet's word in its description so a reader is not told the vendor said SMB. A caliper on the real jack settles it.

the-two-documents-disagree-about-the-cha.note: AND THE DISAGREEMENT IS 80 MM OF DEPTH, not a rounding. The datasheet's Physical section reads "Dimensions (WxDxH): 442 x 509 x 44 mm (17.40 x 20.04 x 1.73 in)". The quick start's own Hardware Specifications table reads "438.4 x 589 x 43.1 mm (17.26 x 23.19 x 1.7 in.)". Both are internally consistent - every inch figure multiplies to its own millimetre figure - so neither is a typo. They describe different boxes. THE DATASHEET IS USED, on three grounds. The live vendor product page agrees with it. Both of the guide's OWN elevations scale to a round 5 px/mm at 442 and to 5.043 and 5.034 at 438.4. And this line's quick starts are shared between models and disclaim their own art in as many words - "The drawings in this document are for illustration only and may not match your particular model" - which is exactly the kind of document whose spec table can be inherited from a neighbour. 438.4 x 589 x 43.1 is very close to the shell edgecore/dcs240 and edgecore/dcs511 sit on. THE WEIGHTS DISAGREE TOO and are recorded the same way: 10.005 kg in the datasheet against "13.48 kg (29.72 lb), with 2 PSUs and 6 fans installed" in the same guide table. The datasheet's figure is used because its dimensions are.
